title: A High-throughput Cell Microarray Platform for Correlative Analysis of Cell Differentiation and Traction Forces
protocol: Immerse glass substrates in 0.25% v/v Triton X-100 in distilled water (dH2O).
Place substrates on an orbital shaker for 30 min.
Rinse substrates 5 times with dH2O after removing Triton X-100 solution.
Immerse substrates in the final rinse and place on an orbital shaker for 30 min.
Remove dH2O and immerse substrates in acetone.
Place substrates on an orbital shaker for 30 min.
Remove acetone and immerse substrates in methanol.
Place substrates on an orbital shaker for 30 min.
Rinse substrates 5 times with dH2O after removing methanol.
Immerse substrates in 0.05 N NaOH and place on an orbital shaker for 1 h.
Remove NaOH solution and rinse substrates 5 times with dH2O.
Dry substrates using filtered compressed air.
Bake substrates at 110 °C on a hot plate until dry (5 – 15 min).
Silanize clean glass substrates.
Immerse clean glass substrates in freshly prepared 2% v/v 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate (3-TPM) in ethanol.
Place substrates on an orbital shaker for 30 min.
Remove 3-TPM solution and immerse substrates in ethanol.
Place substrates on an orbital shaker for 5 min.
Use filtered compressed air to dry the substrates.
Bake at 110 °C on a hot plate until dry (5 – 15 min).
Prepare a pre-polymer solution in dH2O with the desired acrylamide/bisacrylamide percentage (w/v) ratio.
Vortex solution until clear and filter with a 0.2 µm syringe.
Prepare a photoinitiator solution of 20% w/v Irgacure 2959 in methanol.
Mix the pre-polymer and photoinitiator solutions in a 9:1 ratio.
Optionally degas with a vacuum chamber for 15 minutes to remove bubbles.
Pipette 100 µL of the 9:1 pre-polymer:photoinitiator solution onto each silanized slide.
Gently cover each slide with a 22 × 60 mm coverslip while avoiding bubble creation.
Place the drying tray in a UV crosslinker and expose slides to 365 nm UV A for 10 minutes at 4 W/m².
Immerse hydrogels in distilled water (dH₂O) for 5 minutes.
Remove coverslips with a razor, taking care not to damage the polymerized hydrogels.
Leave hydrogels in dH₂O at room temperature for 1 – 3 days, changing dH₂O daily.
Dehydrate hydrogels at 50 °C on a hot plate until dry (15 – 30 minutes).
Store dehydrated hydrogels at room temperature for up to 3 months.
Sonicate a stock solution of 1 µm fluorescent beads for 15 minutes to disperse aggregates.
Prepare a pre-polymer solution in dH2O with the desired acrylamide/bisacrylamide percentage (w/v).
Vortex the solution until clear.
Filter the solution with a 0.2 µm syringe.
Add fluorescent beads to the pre-polymer solution at a final concentration of 0.2% v/v.
Mix the pre-polymer/bead solution and photoinitiator solution in a 9:1 (pre-polymer/bead:photoinitiator) ratio.
Optionally degas the mixture with a vacuum chamber for 15 min to remove bubbles.
Place silanized 35 mm glass-bottom Petri dishes into a glass drying tray.
Pipette 20 μL of 9:1 pre-polymer/bead:photoinitiator solution onto the center of each dish.
Gently cover each slide with a 12 mm circular coverslip while avoiding the creation of bubbles.
Invert the dishes and leave at room temperature for 20 min.
While still inverted, expose dishes to 365 nm UV A for 10 min (4 W/m2).
Immerse hydrogels in 0.1 M HEPES buffer and leave at room temperature in the dark overnight.
Remove coverslips carefully with a razor, taking care not to damage the polymerized hydrogels.
Dehydrate hydrogels at 50 °C on a hot plate until dry (15 – 30 min).
Hydrogels can be stored at room temperature in the dark for 3 months.
Add 164 mg of sodium acetate and 37.2 mg of EDTA to 6 mL dH2O.
Vortex the mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C to thoroughly solubilize.
Add 50 µL of pre-warmed Triton X-100 to the solubilized mixture.
Add 4 mL of glycerol to the mixture.
Vortex and incubate the mixture again at 37 °C to solubilize.
Add 40 – 80 µL of glacial acetic acid, titrating to adjust the pH to 4.8.
Mix 105.5 mg sodium acetate and 37.2 mg EDTA with 6 mL PBS.
Vortex the mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C to thoroughly solubilize.
Add 100 mg CHAPS to the solubilized mixture.
Add 4 mL of glycerol to the mixture.
Combine equal volumes of 2× printing buffer with each biomolecule solution in a 384-well V-bottom microplate at double the target concentration.
Mix each well thoroughly by pipetting, taking care not to generate bubbles.
Centrifuge the source microplate for 1 min at 100 × g.
Clean pins according to the manufacturer's instructions before each microarray fabrication run.
Load clean pins directly into the printhead of the microarrayer.
Turn on the humidifier unit.
Adjust the set point to 65% RH (non-condensing) and wait until the rheometer matches the set point.
Place source plate in the appropriate adaptor.
Dehydrate hydrogel substrates at 50 °C for 15 min.
Place dehydrated hydrogel substrates into the appropriate adaptor.
Adjust parameters of the program to accurately reflect the layout of the source plate, array design, and desired format.
Include wash steps using water between each condition to prevent carry-over and cross-contamination.
Include wash steps using dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) between each condition to prevent carry-over and cross-contamination.
Start array fabrication.
Check no less frequently than once an hour that the humidity has not dropped below 65% RH (non-condensing).
Pause arraying if the humidity drops unexpectedly, fill the humidifier, and clear associated tubes of condensation.
Pause arraying if pins are clogged to clean or replace with pre-cleaned pins.
Place fabricated arrays in a slide box or microplate covered with aluminum foil at room temperature and 65% RH overnight.
Evaluate array quality and retention using general protein stains or immunofluorescence if necessary.
Place arrayed substrates in 4-chambered dishes or 6-well microplates the day after fabrication.
Immerse arrays in 1% v/v penicillin/streptomycin in PBS, using 4 mL for slides and 3 mL for dishes.
Expose arrays to UV C for 30 min.
Exchange penicillin/streptomycin solution with cell culture media.
Collect and count cells.
Seed cells onto arrays at a density of 500 × 10^3 - 2 × 10^6 cells/array, using 4 mL per microscope slide and 3 mL per 35 mm Petri dish.
Incubate array cultures at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2 – 24 h or until well-populated cell islands form.
Wash array cultures twice with pre-warmed cell culture media.
Use 4 mL for slides and 3 mL for dishes during washing.
Aspirate cell culture media from array slides in 4-chambered dishes.
Add 4 mL/slide of freshly prepared 4% v/v paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Aspirate PFA solution and wash each slide 3 times with 4 mL of PBS.
Incubate fixed slides in Triton X-100 for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash each slide 3 times with 4 mL of PBS after incubation.
Add 4 mL/slide of blocking solution (5% v/v serum matched to the species of the secondary antibody) and incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Thoroughly remove blocking solution from each slide.
Add 500 µL/slide of primary antibody diluted in 5% v/v serum in PBS, cover arrays for both 1 h incubations at room temperature as well as overnight incubations at 4 °C.
Wash each array slide 3 times with 4 mL of PBS after incubation.
Add 500 µL/slide of secondary antibody diluted in 5% v/v serum in PBS and cover arrays for both 1 h incubations at room temperature as well as overnight incubations at 4 °C.
Wash each array slide 3 times with 4 mL of PBS after incubation.
Wash briefly with dH2O before carefully removing array slides from solution using forceps.
Pipette 100 µL of mounting solution with DAPI across the slide while confirming complete coverage visually.
Place a 22 × 60 mm coverslip over the slide to mount.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with clear nail polish.
Store in the dark at 4 °C until imaging, no earlier than the next day.
Image entire arrays using either a microarray scanner or inverted fluorescent microscope equipped with a robotic stage.
Save captured images of entire arrays as TIFF files.
Prepare a solution of 1% v/v bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 1% v/v sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in PBS to dissociate cells from substrates during TFM.
Mark the positions (X-coordinate, Y-coordinate) and focus planes (Z-coordinate) of individual cell islands using phase contrast microscopy.
Switch to far red fluorescent microscopy to visualize the beads.
Return to each marked position and correct the Z-coordinate so that only the first layer of beads below the cell island is in focus.
Save the new coordinates.
Proceed to automated imaging of all cell islands for pre-dissociation phase contrast and far red fluorescent images.
Add 150 µL of BSA/SDS solution to the dish and wait 5 min.
Monitor cell dissociation using phase contrast microscopy.
Return to marked positions after cell islands have been dissociated from substrate.
Check that the first layer of beads are in focus; correct Z-coordinate if necessary.
Save corrected Z-coordinates.
Repeat automated imaging of all islands for post-dissociation far red fluorescent images.
Repeat steps for remaining dishes.
Process acquired array images.
Split composite array images into files containing individual channels (i.e., red, blue, or green).
Convert split channel files to 8-bit TIFF images.
Apply binning (e.g., 2×2 or 4×4) to reduce image size to ~32 megapixels per channel.
Note the coordinates in pixels of the top left, bottom left, and bottom right rhodamine-conjugated dextran markers or arrayed conditions.
Use noted coordinates to rotate the 8-bit TIFF images to be perfectly vertical.
Annotate output from single-cell analysis with specific arrayed conditions based on coordinates.
Perform single-cell analysis of binned, rotated 8-bit TIFF images in CellProfiler (version 2.1.1).
Use the IdentifyPrimaryObjects module to identify nuclei.
Use the IdentifySecondaryObjects module to identify immunolabels associated with each cell nucleus.
Use the MeasureObjectIntensity module to quantify nuclear labels and immunolabels.
Export single-cell data from all three modules as a CSV file by channel using the ExportToSpreadsheet module.
Apply quantile normalization by biological replicate to transform data.
Generate a shared distribution across replicates for unbiased comparisons.
Plot cells per island as a combined measure of adhesion and survival.
Calculate and plot the quantile-normalized immunolabel intensity.
Determine percentage of cells positive for an immunolabel above 2 s.d. threshold.
Use consistent negative control mean intensity to set threshold for positivity.
Use ImageJ to batch convert the images to 8-bit TIFF files.
Apply pixel-averaged binning (e.g., 2 × 2) to reduce computational cost and time of downstream analysis.
Input captured phase contrast and far red fluorescent images into MATLAB.
Process images using algorithms developed by Butler et al. and Wang et al.
Select three regions distant from the cell island for accounting image or sample drift.
Provide the factor to convert from pixels to micrometers.
Provide the Young's modulus of the substrate.
Provide the Poisson's ratio.
Draw a boundary around the periphery of each island to define geometrical constraints.
Zero all forces outside the defined boundary for each island.
Calculate the root-mean-square traction stress for each island.
Calculate the contractile moment for each island.
Average root-mean-square values over multiple islands and biological replicates for each arrayed condition.
Calculate associated variance for hypothesis testing.
Average the distribution of stresses or moments over many islands to provide a representative map.
